html:
The Naskapi are an Innu people of the interior of the Quebec-Labrador peninsula in northeastern Canada. They speak a dialect close to Innu-aimun and Cree.

They lived in the northern forest and tundra, following the great caribou herds, which gave them food, clothing, tents and tools. They were closely related to the Montagnais to the south, and the line between the two was drawn mostly by outsiders. Their neighbours to the west were the Cree and on the coast the Inuit.

From the 1800s they traded furs at Hudson's Bay Company posts, which moved them from place to place. Today most live at Kawawachikamach, near Schefferville in Quebec. See also Innu.
